The high, built-up roof sits on concrete and metal decking and is nearly flat with a very low pitch to accommodate proper drainage. Installed along the length of the roof is heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) equipment. The interior is composed of open warehouse space in the northern two-thirds of the building and offices in the southern third. Associated with the building are eight accessory resources: loading dock (AR1), retaining wall (AR2), trailer hookups (AR3-AR4), substations (AR5-AR6), storage boxcar (AR7), and parking lot (AR8). Importantly, there has been no change to the condition of the building exterior and the accessory resources as documented in the original 2021 ARA form. The interior consists of open warehouse space in the northern two-thirds of the building and offices in the southern third. The warehouse space is one large rectangular area that measures 180 ft. long and 100 ft. wide. Modular chain-link fencing is used to divide the interior. Two standalone adjoining offices have been built in the middle of the warehouse space. These two offices are not depicted in a 1969 as-built floor plan (Holmes and Narver) but are shown in a 1990 floor plan (EG&G). There is also a room-sized cold storage cooler on the east wall adjacent to double doors that allow access via the loading dock. The cooler may have held filmic media for EG&G. The only other notable structure is a stationary high-pressure air workstation with a flume hood against the south wall of the open warehouse. This wall serves to separate the warehouse space from the offices. Both the room-sized cold storage cooler and the stationary high-pressure air workstation are denoted on the 1969 as-built floor plan and are part of the original design. Offices in the southern portion of the building are constructed around a U-shaped corridor. In addition to restrooms and a shower room, there are currently 16 offices that vary in size depending on their location around the corridor. Personnel can access the office corridor on either end through pedestrian doors that open via the warehouse or through a double door in the south elevation. The 1969 as-built floor plan indicates that the office space was used for engineers, administrative personnel and functions, records, and a calibration laboratory with an airlock, shielded enclosure, and dark room. The 1990 floor plan shows that by this time all laboratory space had been converted to offices and that some of the office space was subdivided or altered to fit changing needs. Building 06-CP-65 is still being used as a storage and warehouse facility at present. The office space, however, is mostly empty and unused. Character-Defining Features Character-defining features of a building are those that give the building its visual character and can be either exterior or interior elements (Nelson 1988).
